html:
SMTO-MEM-0006 — This memory changed before your change was saved

GUID: 9fa8bc5d-6e78-4526-ad07-c9e28e1bd660
Slug: memory-revision-conflict
Domain: MEM · Subsystem: mem

What happened

  • This memory was changed or deleted somewhere else, possibly by the agent, after you opened it, so SMTO didn't apply your change. The newer saved version was kept.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Copy any text you typed in Content somewhere safe, then select Reload current memory in the Memory Editor. Reloading shows the version saved after you opened the memory, and it replaces what's on screen.
  2. Compare the latest content with your change, re-enter what's still needed, and select Save. SMTO accepts the save once it's based on the version that's saved now.
  3. If the memory is gone after you select Refresh, it was deleted; select New memory to create it again only if you still need it. A deleted memory can't be updated, so your change has to be saved as a new memory.
  4. If the agent reported this error, ask it to read the memory again before updating it. The agent's update was based on an older version and needs the current one.

What success looks like

  • The Memory Editor shows Saved, and the memory's content matches what you intended.

If it still fails

  • If the memory keeps changing under you, a running conversation may be updating it; wait for that task to finish, then try again. Don't delete the memory just to get past this. If it continues, send the copied error details to the person who manages SMTO.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A conditional Memory update or delete failed in MemoryStore._compare because the entry no longer exists or its current revision differs from expected_revision.

What this means

  • A conditional Memory update/delete finds no current entry or a revision different from expected_revision. Memory validation and conditional writes preserve the current stored revision on rejection. This is global Memory, separate from conversation KV; diagnostic rendering does not perform additional storage operations.

Why this can happen

  • A conditional Memory update/delete finds no current entry or a revision different from expected_revision.

How to diagnose it

  • Read the current exact key/value/revision and reconsider the intended change against it.

How to fix it

  • Re-read the entry (memory.get, or Reload current memory in the Memory Editor) to get its current value and revision, merge the intended change, and resubmit with that revision as expected_revision. Do not drop expected_revision to force the write.
  • Read the current value and revision, then update or delete against that exact revision.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • A deliberate update uses the current revision without removing concurrency protection.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • Memory validation and conditional writes preserve the current stored revision on rejection. This is global Memory, separate from conversation KV; diagnostic rendering does not perform additional storage operations.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.

Do not confuse with / related errors

  • SMTO-FIL-0025 — A file changed while SMTO was working with it
  • SMTO-FIL-0027 — SMTO lost its place while reading a file in parts
  • SMTO-KV-0006 — A scratch note changed before the Agent could update it
